250387238_1454e2c0.text: In the hilus of the dentate gyrus, different classification schemes of GABAergic interneurons have been proposed, based on morphological features, neuropeptides and calcium-binding proteins contents or electrophysiological behaviors (Houser, 2007) (Freund et al., 1998)(Lübke et al., 1998)(Mott et al., 1997)(Han et al., 1993)(Halasy et al., 1993)(Acsády et al., 2000)(Buckmaster et al., 1995)(Jinno et al., 2002)
250387238_1454e2c0.section: Classical Functional and Morphological Interneuron Types

250387238_9cab36d0.text: At the molecular level, these classes are well defined based on the expression of calcium binding proteins such as parvalbumin (PV) and calretinin (CR), and neuropeptides like somatostatin (SOM), Neuropeptide Y (NPY) and cholecystokinin (CCK), and enzymes such as the neuronal NO synthase (NOS1)
250387238_9cab36d0.section: Classical Functional and Morphological Interneuron Types

250387238_499cc4fb.text: Most GABAergic interneurons populating the neocortex, hippocampus and striatum share a common developmental origin (Pelkey et al., 2017)(Hu et al., 2017)(Lim et al., 2018)(Villar‐Cerviño et al., 2015). Accordingly, they tend to include the same 3 major families: (1) soma and axo-axonic neurons showing fast discharge and expressing PV, (2) dendrite targeting interneurons expressing SOM and (3) neurogliaform neurons expressing NPY/ Reelin (Kawaguchi et al., 1997)[27](Tremblay et al., 2016)(Tepper et al., 2010) (Tepper et al., 2018)(Klausberger et al., 2008). Regions of the cortex and hippocampus also include soma targeting interneurons expressing CCK and interneurons expressing VIP projecting to other types of inhibitory cells (Pelkey et al., 2017)(Tremblay et al., 2016).
